items.claim: The close of MT 18:5-18:9 is correctly grounded: חָיֹ֣ה יִֽחְיֶ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה stands byte-exact and verse-final at MT 18:9, and that is the only verse-final occurrence of the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH formula in MT 18. Two facts around it are short. First, the parenthetical contrasting it with the formula's mid-verse recurrences in MT 18 names two verses, while the formula also stands mid-verse at MT 18:3 and at MT 18:32 - four mid-verse occurrences, not two, and the omission understates the very contrast the close rests on. Second, the setumah after MT 18:4 is the onset's far-side corroboration and is argued in prose only; it is not carried among the row's boundary evidence refs, although the other five rows of this span each carry their far-side mark there. The absence sentence itself is true and is not a false-absence claim: MT 18:5-18:9 carries no parashah mark, no ketiv/qere note, no paseq occurrence and no editorial note, and the setumah sits at MT 18:4, outside the span.
items.both_sides: Onset side: a setumah stands after MT 18:4, closing the thesis verse, and MT 18:5 opens the first case with no onset formula - a default case-law onset with mark corroboration from the far side. Close side: MT 18:9 ends with the utterance formula, the sole verse-final instance of it in the chapter, and MT 18:10 resumes the case series with no onset formula and no mark. No parashah mark falls at MT 18:9, so the close rests on the formula's verse-final position, which the bytes support and which no other verse in MT 18 shares.

That holds for the inventoried formulae and for the marks, none of which falls in MT 18:10-18:19, but the life clause חָיֹ֥ה יִחְיֶֽה stands verse-final at MT 18:17 and again at MT 18:19 - closural repetition inside the span that the row's device disclosure does not record and that its rejection reasoning, which weighs only a cut before MT 18:14, does not weigh. items.claim: The row's substrate signals assert the as-I-live oath for MT 18:21-18:23. That oath does not stand in this span: within MT 18 and MT 19 it occurs once only, at MT 18:3, two rows back. What the span does carry, at MT 18:23, is the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH formula, sitting mid-verse - which the row's prose describes correctly and its signal list omits. The boundary itself is sound and the Hebrew facts hold: וְהָרָשָׁ֗ע כִּ֤י יָשׁוּב֙ opens MT 18:21 byte-exact, the whole of MT 18:23 collates exactly, a setumah stands after MT 18:20 and another after MT 18:23, the span's single ketiv/qere note is at MT 18:21 with the written form standing unpointed in the running text, no paseq occurrence and no editorial note lies inside the span, and the row is right to refuse a verse-final reading of the MT 18:23 formula, since a further clause follows it in that verse.

Close side: a setumah stands after MT 18:23, where the rhetorical question completes; the utterance formula inside that verse is mid-verse, so the mark and the content close carry the seam rather than formula position, exactly as the row argues. Both sides of this three-verse row are marked, and that is what carries so short an extent.

items.claim: Three facts are wrong while the boundary is right. First, the row reports the editors' note at MT 18:29 as flagging the objection's form against BHS; the note says the reverse - that BHS has been faithful to the Leningrad Codex where the validity of the form might be questioned and that the editors keep the same form as BHS. It records agreement, not divergence, and it is the only editorial note in MT 18-19. Second, the row's substrate signals assert a messenger formula for MT 18:27-18:32; the thus-says-the-Lord-YHWH messenger formula stands in no verse of MT 18 or MT 19 at all. Third, the same list asserts a formula-final close at MT 18:32, while the row's own reading of the bytes - correct - is that the utterance formula there is mid-verse and that the closing imperative clause and the petuchah carry the close; content-final is the key the bytes support, and it is the key used elsewhere in this span for exactly this situation. The Hebrew itself checks out: MT 18:27's opening words, MT 18:30's opening clause and MT 18:32's final clause וְהָשִׁ֖יבוּ וִֽחְיֽוּ collate exactly, the written form at MT 18:28 stands unpointed in the running text, and no paseq occurrence lies in the span.
items.both_sides: Onset side: a setumah stands after MT 18:26 and MT 18:27 opens the positive repentance case with no onset formula. Close side: a petuchah stands after MT 18:32 at the chapter's end, with the utterance formula mid-verse in that verse and the closing imperative clause after it. Both seams are mark-corroborated. The interior turn at MT 18:30 is rightly not cut: the pattern that licenses an internal cut on a fresh therefore is a refrain close standing immediately before it, and MT 18:29 ends with the objection rather than a refrain, with no mark between the two verses.

suggested_fix.fact: the editorial note at MT 18:29 records that the editors keep the same form as BHS, following the Leningrad Codex where the form's validity could be questioned - an agreement note, not a flag against BHS; the messenger formula stands in no verse of MT 18-19; and the close at MT 18:32 is content-final, the utterance formula in that verse being mid-verse

items.claim: The English beside the MT 19:10 splice renders the word after the vine simile as in your vineyard. The spliced word is בְּדָמְךָ֖, in your blood, and the translation held on file for this book renders it in your blood as well. A vineyard reading is a conjectural emendation the witness does not carry, so a byte-exact splice is presented under a rendering of a different word - the one place in this row where the Hebrew and the English part company. Everything else holds: MT 19:1 and MT 19:14 are byte-exact whole verses, the lament noun stands once at MT 19:1 and twice in the colophon at MT 19:14, a petuchah stands after MT 18:32, after MT 19:9 and after MT 19:14, no ketiv/qere note and no editorial note touches MT 19, the fourteen-verse whole-chapter extent is disclosed with its density and carries both the lowered confidence and the flag a whole-chapter extent calls for, and the close at MT 19:14 does end the undated collection that opens on the word-event at MT 12:1.
items.both_sides: Onset side: a petuchah stands after MT 18:32, closing the chapter before, and MT 19:1 opens with the lament command, an onset class in its own right - neither a word-event formula nor a son-of-man address, as the row states truthfully. Close side: a petuchah stands after MT 19:14, whose last clause names the composition a lament for the second and third time in the chapter, and the next verse opens a dated scene. The internal petuchah after MT 19:9 is disclosed and rightly not taken as a row seam: a lament-labelled unit is not split, and the vine stanza from MT 19:10 falls inside the colophon's frame.

unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: This is one more instance of the read-form rendering question already routed to the controlling agent. The written form and the substantive variant disclosure are both correct, so nothing in the row's argument turns on it; what a ruling needs is the sites and their count, and this is one of them. The other three read forms in this cluster, at MT 18:21, MT 18:24 and MT 18:28, are not rendered at all - only the written forms are quoted, and each of those is an exact copy of the running text.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The row covering MT 19 carries a parable-class figure-shift signal for a chapter whose only genre label is the lament noun, at MT 19:1 and twice at MT 19:14. The parable noun does not occur in MT 19; the two parable-root forms in the chapter, at MT 19:11 and MT 19:14, are the ruling sense rather than the genre word. Whether that signal class is licensed for a lament-labelled unit is a taxonomy question rather than a byte question, so it is recorded rather than filed as a defect.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The figure shift from lions to vine is real and the row argues it from bytes; only the key's class is in question. If the parable class is meant for units the text itself labels a parable, the key needs replacing wherever a lament row carries it, which is a corpus-wide decision and not one row's fix.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The cut between MT 18:9 and MT 18:10 falls inside a single word-event unit and rests on a refrain close alone - the verse-final utterance formula at MT 18:9 - with no adjacent parashah mark and with no fresh therefore at the onset, which is the pairing named where an internal cut rests on a refrain close.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: This lane supports the cut: the close is a tier-1 formula and it is the chapter's only verse-final instance, so the evidence is textual and not formatting-derived. But the pattern named for an internal cut pairs the refrain close with a following therefore, and this seam has the close without the pairing. Worth a ruling if the same pattern recurs elsewhere in the book.
